searchText: Kiln Spec v2 is now available! 🔥🧱 It comes with the following major updates: - Engine API Auth - `engine_exchangeTransitionConfigurationV1` - EIP-4399: Rename `RANDOM` to `PREVRANDAO` Change set: https://hackmd.io/@n0ble/kiln-spec#v2-change-set I may have missed in some threads: given the JWT authentication, any ideas on supporting https on `engine_` endpoint? <@!425572898787426305> we have an internal debate about calling.`engine_exchangetransitionconfigurationv1` is necessary post merge for heart beat. What are the implications that we don't call `engine_exchangetransitionconfigurationv1`regularily and just let state transition fails? Is it possible that EL node can trick CL node into doing even worse stuff? Curiosity, if we do not need block rewards post merge why we keep 0.3 eth of reward? And not 0? <dannyryan> why do we not need block rewards? <dannyryan> it’s just that the ongoing costs of PoW (hardware depreciation and energy costs) are not there so the amount paid for same security can be much lower <dannyryan> and it’s not 0.3 per block, the amount issued is a function of the validator set size and scales at the sqrt(num_vals) oh okay thank you, and is it given in the form of beacon ethers not actual EL ethers, is that right? There are no beacon ethers or EL ethers. Just ethers such as miners get them for mining blocks. Is there an EIP about it ? <dannyryan> PoS issues ETH to validators on the beacon chain (to thir validator balance). Once validation of a particular validator is complete (and withdrawals are enabled) validator deposits plus additional issued ETH could be withdrawn into the execution layer https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3675#block-and-ommer-rewards states that the block/ommer rewards are deprecated Note: Transaction fee mechanics affecting the block’s beneficiary account MUST remain unchanged. I just want to know who / how fee mechanism is defined. Eip ? I have been searching / asking / reading still do not get to it. I guess I should try harder. <dannyryan> the yellow paper defines how TX fees go to the beneficiery <dannyryan> this logic remains unchanged <dannyryan> defined in the yellowpaper here — https://ethereum.github.io/yellowpaper/paper.pdf <dannyryan> essentially, TX fees still go to the beneficiery <dannyryan> (less the burn introduced in 1559) May I DM you dannyryan ?

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content:
Kiln Spec v2  is now available! 🔥🧱

It comes with the following major updates:
- Engine API Auth
- `engine_exchangeTransitionConfigurationV1`
- EIP-4399: Rename `RANDOM` to `PREVRANDAO`

Change set: https://hackmd.io/@n0ble/kiln-spec#v2-change-set

excerpts.author: tbenr
excerpts.content: I may have missed in some threads: given the JWT authentication, any ideas on supporting https on `engine_` endpoint?

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: <@!425572898787426305> we have an internal debate about calling.`engine_exchangetransitionconfigurationv1` is necessary post merge for heart beat. What are the implications that we don't call `engine_exchangetransitionconfigurationv1`regularily and just let state transition fails? Is it possible that EL node can trick CL node into doing even worse stuff?

excerpts.content: Curiosity, if we do not need block rewards post merge why we keep 0.3 eth of reward?

excerpts.content: And not 0?

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <dannyryan> why do we not need block rewards?

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <dannyryan> it’s just that the ongoing costs of PoW (hardware depreciation and energy costs) are not there so the amount paid for same security can be much lower

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <dannyryan> and it’s not 0.3 per block, the amount issued is a function of the validator set size and scales at the sqrt(num_vals)

excerpts.author: funnygiulio
excerpts.content: oh okay thank you, and is it given in the form of beacon ethers not actual EL ethers, is that right?

excerpts.author: kedos25.eth
excerpts.content: There are no beacon ethers or EL ethers. Just ethers such as miners get them for mining blocks.
